transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-19
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Sophie Rao (Redwood CSM), Rajiv Menon (Lighthawk Head of Cloud), Elena Garcia (Platform Eng), Tom Price (InfoSec), Anika Bose (Product), Joon Park (SRE)
Links shared: Redwood onboarding deck (link: drive.redwood.example/marketplace-onboard), sample helm chart (link: github.com/redwood/sample-helm), Lighthawk preflight doc (internal)

Topics: packaging & listing artifacts, UAT environment, VPC/KMS, billing hooks, certification runbook

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um I think we've got all the right folks, quick agenda — packaging requirements for marketplace, uat pilot timeline, security questions and then next steps
00:22 Rajiv: yep that's right, our aim is to have a minimal pilot up in your marketplace with a private listing and basic billing so we can validate install flows, and then a broader GA listing later. timeline is tight, 3 weeks ideally
00:41 Liam: cool, we can get the minimal helm/arm artifacts together — just to flag we have a sample helm chart that people usually start from, it sets up the nodepool, serviceaccount, rbac and the redwood runtime as a k8s deployment
01:05 Elena: quick question, for private listings do you expect us to run a sidecar or is this a full in-cluster service? like are we shipping an operator or a helm chart?
01:20 Liam: good q — typically we recommend helm + operator optional. operator is for big customers, for pilot helm alone is fine. the important bits are values for gpu nodeSelector and kv cache persistence 
01:44 Tom: security wise, we need to understand KMS integration. do you talk to Redwoods KMS or our cloud KMS? we can't have keys leaving our control
02:10 Maya: absolutely — Redwood Private/P r i v e t supports customer-managed KMS. sorry my typo there — you can bring your own K M S, we only store encrypted blobs and rotation is customer-controlled. we'll share the KMS integration note
02:33 Tom: also need to see audit logs, SSO/SAML flows and RBAC mapping, plus data residency info
02:48 Sophie: we have a security pack that covers SOC 2, ISO and KMS flow diagrams; we'll attach that. some of the words in the docs are generic but you can mark the sensitive bits
03:10 Anika: from product, we want to test the model routing fallback — for example defaulting to a cheaper variant if capacity is constrained. can that be set in the listing config?
03:32 Liam: yes, we have routing policy metadata that can be embedded in the listing manifest. for pilot you can just toggle a fallback boolean, later we support region and latency policies
03:56 Joon: network question: will we need VPC peering or can we do ingress via an ALB? we prefer peering if possible for lower latencies
04:15 Maya: both options supported. for dedicated/private customers, VPC peering is common; for hosted marketplace we often use an ingress + mTLS. we'll send sample firewall rules and IP ranges
04:40 Elena: any special ports for KV cache or the runtime?
04:50 Liam: runtime speaks on 443 for API, ter-- sorry, there's also an internal metrics port 9100 open for Prometheus scraping if you enable it. KV cache uses gRPC on 7070 by default, sometimes shows up as k V cash in transcripts, ha
05:12 Rajiv: regarding billing — what's the charging model for marketplace listing? per-token or seat? how do we map usage back to Lighthawk org?
05:30 Maya: marketplace billing depends on the marketplace vendor. we instrument per-request token counts and provide metering hooks. for this pilot we'll provide a CSV-based metering export and a webhook for events; if you go full listing we'll integrate the metering connector for automated billing
05:55 Tom: we need to ensure metering events don't leak PII and are hashed appropriately
06:10 Liam: metering payloads are limited to request id, model id, token counts, region. payloads can be configured to omit user identifiers
06:30 Anika: for UAT, can we test a meager load? like 50 concurrent sessions to validate batching and cold-starts
06:44 Liam: yes we can simulate that; we'll provide a small load script and a profile for how the runtime will behave with batching enabled
07:02 Maya: next up let's walk through the packaging checklist — do we have the chart, the values, and the manifest?
07:18 Elena: we have a chart skeleton, but need the recommended values for autoscaling and the quantization profiles; otherwise we get OOMs on smaller nodes
07:33 Liam: recommended values: start with 2 replicas for the inference service, request/limit set to 8g/12g for gpu-sim nodes, autoscaler based on queue depth, and a quantization profile named q3-f16 for cost saving. we'll send concrete values
07:58 Rajiv: do you provide GPU images or do we build from your Dockerfile?
08:12 Liam: we publish certified images and also provide a base Dockerfile so you can rebuild if you need private registry. image tags are semver'd and pinned in the manifest
08:32 Maya: let's address the certification runbook — the listing needs a smoke test, a security checklist, and a UAT signoff. Sophie, can you outline the steps?
08:44 Sophie: sure — smoke test: deploy chart, run smoke traffic (10 requests), verify health endpoints, verify KV cache persistence; security checklist: KMS config, RBAC, SSO integration; UAT signoff: product owner gives go/no-go after 48 hrs of UAT
09:10 Tom: we also require pen test results or an attestation — do you have a standard attestation we can include in procurement?
09:25 Maya: yes we have an attestation template and SOC-2 report excerpt, we'll share the redacted report via secure link
09:40 Rajiv: timeline — if we target the cluster up by next monday, when can Redwood do a deploy?
09:52 Liam: we can do an initial deploy as soon as you open access, I'd say 48 hours after cluster is ready to allow us to validate values and tweak image pulls
10:10 Anika: who owns the e2e tests in UAT? we want Redwood to run the smoke and then our QA to run product tests
10:22 Maya: Redwood SE will run smoke, then handoff to your QA with a test plan. we'll provide test scripts and the load script.
10:35 Joon: on monitoring, we need to feed metrics into our prometheus and also see tracing — is there an opentelemetry pipeline?
10:50 Liam: yes otel exporters are supported; we can configure otlp over collector. logs are written to stdout and you can grab them with fluentd to your ELK
11:12 Elena: small nit — any restrictions on node types in the marketplace? some vendors insist on specific instance families
11:25 Maya: we list recommended types in the manifest, but you can override. for performance predictability we recommend a fixed family for quantized workloads
11:40 Tom: compliance question — do you rotate keys automatically if we use customer KMS? we need to show key rotation logs for audits
11:52 Liam: rotation is driven by your KMS policies; we will log encryption events but key lifecycle remains in your control
12:08 Rajiv: ok, let's talk about the UAT acceptance criteria — what metrics do we want to capture? latency p50/p95, error rate, cost per 1k tokens?
12:26 Anika: yes p50/p95 and a qualitative check on generation quality — compare a fixed prompt set between the hosted variant and a cheaper fallback
12:45 Liam: we'll produce a comparison report and attach thresholds for p95 under 600ms for short prompts, and error rate under 1% during the 50-concurrency run
13:02 Maya: any blockers we haven't covered?
13:10 Tom: need to ensure legal has the attestation and data processing addendum, will ping procurement after I review
13:22 Rajiv: network allowlist — we'll share network diagram and open the IPs you listed. Joon will coordinate with Liam on the peering window
13:36 Liam: noted, I'll provide a small script to check connectivity and certs before deploy
13:50 Anika: just flagging that product may want a canary rollout so we can A/B with current infra on day one
14:05 Liam: canary supported — we'll include a rollout manifest and a toggle in the values to set weight
14:20 Sophie: to recap actions: Maya to share deck & security pack; Liam to share helm values & deploy script; Tom to share network diagram & KMS requirements; Elena to create UAT cluster; Rajiv to validate timeline. We'll loop up on the 26th for the pilot deploy check-in
14:45 Maya: perfect, thanks all. I'll send minutes and the checklist after this call
15:00 Rajiv: thanks, will wait for the artifacts
15:10 Elena: thanks everyone
15:18 (meeting ends)

Notes/on artifacts: sample helm repo referenced: github.com/redwood/sample-helm (contains values-prod.yaml, values-uat.yaml, rollout-manifest.yaml). Security pack: redwood-sec-pack-v2.pdf (shared link). Metering connector spreadsheet: redwood-metering-v1.csv (mapping tokens->billing buckets).

Post-call scribbles (imperfections): occasional mis-typo of Redwood Private as 'Redwood Privet', KMS sometimes written out as K M S, KV cache said aloud like K V cash, 'sock-two' appears in one sentence when talking about SOC 2, minor drops in speaker attribution where Speaker X was used for 2 seconds but corrected after.
